lines.trans: Oh, Jindi, hide this knife quickly!
Why should I hide this knife?
This is our chef's favorite knife!
The chef has been looking for it all morning.
I simply wanted to wash dishes.
If the chef sees the knife, there will be a scandal!
He will yell at us very loudly.
What should I do now?
Put the knife back onto the table.
Let the chef find his knife himself.
Hide it further away from here, quickly!
Alright, I will put everything away now.

words.gloss: to remove, to take away; to tidy up

lines.trans: Just do not say anything to anyone!

words.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

words.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'faster'.
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to shout', forming an aspectual pair with 'крикнуть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Secondary conversational sense ('beloved, darling') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('oh') used directly in spoken exchanges.
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: comparative of далеко with prefix по-

examples.trans: Stand a little further back behind the pines.
Step a little further away from the fire.

examples.text: Иван, встань подальше, вон там за соснами.
examples.trans: Ivan, stand further back, over there behind the pines.

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'класть'.

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

examples.text: А вот сюда я её и положу! Отличный подарок будет!
examples.trans: Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мыть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wash', forming an aspectual pair with 'мыть'.

meanings.en: dishes, plates and cups, tableware (collective singular)
meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'dishes', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Get up and go wash the dishes!
Clean tableware is on the table.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hide', forming an aspectual pair with 'спрятать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Преступники прятали у слепых плохую траву!
examples.trans: Criminals were hiding bad herbs at the blind society!
What are you hiding behind your back?

examples.text: Пишут, что преступники прятали у слепых плохую траву!
examples.trans: They write that criminals were hiding bad herbs at the blind society!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'scandal', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A scandal began in the restaurant dining room.
There is no need to make a scene.

examples.text: Если шеф увидит нож, будет скандал!
examples.trans: If the chef sees the knife, there will be a scandal!

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прятать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hide', paired with 'прятать'.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'table', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: We will sit together in a friendly way at the table.

examples.text: Не бойся, всё в порядке! Посидим дружно за столом.
examples.trans: Don't be afraid, everything is fine! We will sit together in a friendly way at the table.
Take your feet off the table quickly!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

убрать.gloss: to remove, to take away; to tidy up

meanings.en: to remove, to take away, to cut out
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to remove', forming an aspectual pair with 'убирать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to clean up, to tidy') (a room) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Take the phone off the table.

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
